title: Switching lemma corollary for CNF formulas
statement:
Fix $n \ge 1$ and let $\psi$ be a CNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, meaning every clause of $\psi$ has at most $w$ literals; assume moreover that no clause of $\psi$ repeats a literal or uses a variable in two of its literals, and that $5s \le n$. Call a restriction $\rho$ that leaves exactly $s$ of the $n$ variables free \emph{bad} if the restricted function $x \mapsto \psi(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ is computed by no DNF formula of width at most $w$. Then the number $B$ of bad restrictions satisfies
\[
  B \cdot n^{w} \;\le\; \binom{n}{s}\, 2^{\,n-s} \, (10\,s\,w)^{w}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: ψ is a CNF formula on n variables
ψ has width at most w
no clause uses a variable in two literals (same var ⇒ same literal)
counts restrictions with exactly s free variables
bad = restricted function not computed by any DNF of width ≤ w
replaced:
For a CNF $\psi$ of width at most $w$ with $5s \leq n$ and well-formed clauses, the
number of $s$-restrictions $\rho$ for which $\psi|_\rho$ cannot be represented by a
DNF of width $\leq w$ satisfies
\[
  \abs{\{\rho : \mathrm{IsRestriction}\,s\,\rho \wedge \lnot\,\exists \varphi,\ \varphi.\mathrm{width} \leq w \wedge \varphi \equiv \psi|_\rho\}} \cdot n^w
  \;\leq\; \mathrm{numSRestrictions}\,n\,s \cdot (10\,s\,w)^w .
\]
